results.diagnosis: The add function is using subtraction operator instead of addition operator.
The discount calculation does not divide discount_percent by 100, causing it to multiply the full discount_percent value instead of the decimal percentage.
The condition uses > instead of >= so a score of exactly 60 incorrectly returns False when it should return True.
The function reverses individual characters in the string instead of reversing the order of words.
The range function starts from 0 instead of 1, causing the sum to exclude 1 and include 0, resulting in 10 instead of 15 for sum_up_to(5).
Mutable default argument persists across function calls, causing items to accumulate instead of starting fresh each time.
The function does not convert words to lowercase before counting, causing different case variations of the same word to be counted separately.
The base case only checks for n == 1, but should also handle n == 0, causing infinite recursion when factorial(0) is called since 0! = 1 by mathematical definition.
The function does not handle division by zero and should return 0 when the divisor is 0.
The parse_age function raises ValueError and TypeError for invalid inputs instead of returning 0 as expected by the tests.
The function uses an off-by-one index error: items[len(items)] should be items[len(items) - 1] or items[-1], and must handle empty lists by returning None.
The function uses direct dictionary access user_dict["email"] which raises a KeyError when the "email" key is missing, but it should return None instead.
The function uses the union operator (|) instead of the intersection operator (&), returning all elements from both lists instead of only the common elements.
The function converts the username to lowercase but forgets to strip leading and trailing whitespace.
The base case checks if n == 1 instead of n == 0, causing infinite recursion when factorial(0) is called since 0 never matches the base case condition.
The loop condition `while low < high:` prevents checking the last remaining element when low equals high, causing the function to return -1 for elements at the end or in single-element arrays.
The function crashes with ZeroDivisionError when given an empty list because it attempts division by zero without checking if the list is empty first.
The function doesn't convert the input text to lowercase before checking for buzzwords, causing case-sensitive mismatches with words like "Passionate" or "NINJA".
